review_policy: Full authoritative document, registered feature semantics, entity/counterparty roles, row cutoff, and overlap with accepted canonical facts were reviewed. Candidate assertions were not treated as authoritative.

decisions.reason: Alphabet's timely Form 10-Q reports the quarter-end total notional backstop exposure and defines it as maximum potential payments for third-party data-center leases. This is the required total-stock scope, not a project component.

Meta's timely Form 10-Q explicitly reports a newly entered October aggregate for multi-year third-party cloud-capacity arrangements. The disclosure is customer-side contract flow and does not reuse the previously accepted September CoreWeave contract.

The $333 million is one project component, not Alphabet's latest total backstop stock. Promoting it as the total-stock feature would replace the broader $6.529 billion disclosure with a narrower scope.
The $81.19 billion total mixes cloud capacity, servers, networking, Reality Labs hardware, and data centers. It cannot be attributed wholly to the registered cloud-contract-flow feature.
The February 2026 filing was not publicly available by the November 2025 row cutoff and states general corporate purpose rather than attributable AI debt.
